newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday after long-position holders were seen liquidating, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 23,300 yuan ($2,809) per tonne, losing 160 yuan.
It opened at 23,400 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,450 and a low of 23,250 yuan per tonne. July lost 60 to 22,740, August 150 to 22,910, September 240 to 23,080 and November 190 to 23,370.
Combined volume rose to 53,370 tonnes from 51,730 tonnes.
Copper opened lower but mostly at intraday highs, and then fell for most of the session.
Traders said many investors were eager to liquidate their long positions due to weak market sentiment.

"Long liquidation was responsible for today's falls with many investors believing a downward trend has already started," one trader said. "Falling copper demand with the summer season approaching is another factor."
Physical values are soft on weak demand, traders said, with prices indicated at around 22,900 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said active stock trading in the past few days had seen some speculative funds leave copper and flow back to the share markets. This had helped depress prices on Monday.
The expected arrival in Shanghai in the next couple of days of 5,000 tonnes of copper, taken from Singapore warehouses run by the London Metal Exchange, added to the gloom, traders said.
They said they expected the falls to continue for the coming few trading days.
Aluminium ended sharply down. July fell 360 to 14,330, August 400 to 14,400 and September 450 to 14,500 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 1,640 tonnes from 2,930 tonnes.
